title: Network Security Groups
description: Learn how Network Security Groups act as firewalls for your Azure subnets and network interfaces.

data.text: A Network Security Group (NSG) contains a list of security rules that allow or deny inbound and outbound network traffic. You can attach an NSG to a subnet or a network interface.
Rules are evaluated by priority — lower numbers are checked first. Once a rule matches, no further rules are evaluated.

data.title: NSG Rule Properties
items: Name — friendly label for the rule
Source / Destination — IP, CIDR, service tag, or app security group

data.title: Create an NSG and Add Rules (Azure CLI)
data.content: Create an NSG that allows HTTPS inbound and denies all other inbound traffic.
data.code:
az network nsg create   --name myNsg   --resource-group myRG

az network nsg rule create   --nsg-name myNsg   --resource-group myRG   --name Allow-HTTPS   --priority 100   --direction Inbound   --access Allow   --protocol Tcp   --destination-port-range 443   --source-address-prefixes Internet

az network nsg rule create   --name Deny-All-Inbound   --nsg-name myNsg   --resource-group myRG   --priority 4096   --direction Inbound   --access Deny   --source-address-prefixes "*"   --destination-port-range "*"

data.title: Lock Down a Web Subnet
data.description: Create an NSG that allows only HTTP and HTTPS from the internet and allows SSH from your IP only.
steps: Add an inbound rule allowing TCP 80 and 443 from any source.
Add an inbound rule allowing TCP 22 from your public IP.
Add a deny-all rule at the end.
Associate the NSG with your web subnet.
data.expectedOutcome: Your web subnet accepts only web traffic and your SSH access.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NSGs act as stateless firewalls at the subnet or NIC level.
Rules are evaluated by priority, first match wins.
Always end with a deny-all rule for defense in depth.
